bull.b: Q2 revenue growth and the shift to positive operating income and adjusted EBITDA show improved performance across core segments. If sustained, stronger volumes and gross profit could support reinvestment and gradually improve the company’s ability to fund expansion.

The dairy RNG platform combines operating infrastructure with a sizeable contracted feedstock base, supporting multi-year capacity growth. Approved and pending low-carbon pathways may also increase credit generation per unit, strengthening the economics of future RNG production.

The MVR project could structurally lower operating costs while reducing carbon intensity and improving eligibility value for 45Z and LCFS credits. Its expected cash-flow contribution would materially improve plant economics once commissioning is completed by the end of 2026.

bear.b: Deeply negative equity and rising debt indicate limited balance-sheet flexibility and increase refinancing exposure. The leverage burden can absorb future operating cash flow through interest and principal obligations, constraining investment capacity and reducing resilience if projects or credit proceeds are delayed.

bear.t: Persistent cash burn and tight liquidity
bear.b: Negative operating and free cash flow show that the business is not yet self-funding, while only $1.0 million of quarter-end cash leaves little buffer for working capital or project needs. Continued external funding or asset-level cash receipts therefore remains important to maintain operations.

A meaningful portion of expected value depends on regulatory calculations and approvals that remain uncertain in timing and scope. Delays or less favorable treatment could reduce credit proceeds, defer cash realization, and weaken the economics supporting planned growth and debt refinancing.
